messages:
sara: Midday batch window — seeing an unexpected p95 jump between rack-g17 and rack-g29 around 12:05. Latency spikes ~200-450ms, short lived but coincides with batch ramp. packet counters showing bursty drops. anyone else seeing RDMA retransmits?
ryan: yep spotted it too. NV_peerlink logs show retransmits and some `psm2` errors. not constant, comes in waves. :grimacing:
maria: saw redispatch churn on scheduler around same time. KV-cache warmups line up with the first few spikes. possible interplay between cache misses + larger batch windows? :thinking:
sara: attaching quick tcpdump snippet from g17->g29 (trimmed):
```
12:05:03.123 IP g17 > g29: seq 12345 ack 67890 flags [P.] length 1200
12:05:03.125 IP g17 > g29: frag 1/2 len 800
12:05:03.126 IP g17 > g29: frag 2/2 len 400
12:05:03.200 [RETRANS] g17 > g29: seq 12345
```
nate: frag/mtu clues. are these racks on different ToR models? we had an older ToR at rack-g29 until last month.
ryan: confirmed — rack-g29 still on tor-b-1 (firmware 3.4.0). other racks moved to tor-b-2 (3.7.1) last quarter. I see PMTU discovery probe failures in the switch logs.
maria: that could explain fragmentation + reassembly delay under high batch coalescence. when batch size increases, we push bigger frames and hit fragmentation boundary more often.
oncall: oncall here — temporarily rate-limiting large inter-node batches might be quickest mitigation. can we throttle to 80% for the next 15m and observe?
sara: I'll open a canary policy on the job with `--max-batch-tokens=1024` (was 1600) and pin to the affected zone.
ryan: also raising `net.ipv4.tcp_no_fragment` to 1 on the nodes would surface PMTU failures faster while we track the switches. planning to roll to a small subset.
maria: logging note — capture `ethtool -S eth0` around the spike window and collect `psm2` stats on both sides. may help differentiate NIC drops vs switch-level fragmentation.
sara: quick snippet from `dmesg` on g29 during the spike: 
```
[12:05:03] mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: NIC QP rx error, cq overrun
[12:05:03] psm2: retransmit timeout on qp 42
```
nate: ugh, cq overrun. that points to bursting into a saturated RX queue on the NIC. Could be driver or qpair config.
ryan: we tried bumping RX ring from 1024->2048 on one node last week for perf testing, remember? maybe mismatch with older ToR buffering makes it worse.
sara: Action plan: 1) throttle batch tokens in affected AZ for 30m, 2) capture `ethtool -S` + `psm2` on both endpoints for next spike, 3) ask network team to check PMTU/firmware on tor-b-1, 4) consider temporary batch spread (shard batches across racks) if spikes persist.
maria: tagging @oncall and @nate for rollout help. also adding a metric dashboard for `qp_retransmits` and `rx_cq_overruns` to the incident panel.
oncall: doing throttle now. will monitor dashboards and escalate to network if spikes continue after 15m. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy job batch-service-canary started by sara — job_id=svc-canary-2026-03-20-1208
ryan: preliminary observation after throttling: p95 dropped to ~35ms within 2 minutes. still seeing tiny retransmit blips but no big jolt. looks promising.
sara: good. can we collect one more full run with packet capture + ethtool + qpair stats? will hand to network for triage.
nate: I'll script the captures and push to S3 with a small manifest. putting logs under `s3://redwood-infra/incident/3321114321/`.
maria: long-term: we should consider explicit path MTU checks during deployment window and a hardware inventory rule to avoid mixing older ToR firmware with newer NIC configs in a single batch pool.
sara: agreed. adding follow-up ticket for inventory and firmware rollouts. thanks all for the quick responses. :pray:
